title: Usage event marshaller and soft-typing adapter
creator: Asha Menon
description: Introduce a lightweight marshalling service that normalizes heterogeneous usage events into a canonical, typed envelope while applying configurable soft-typing/coercion rules. The goal is to reduce hard rejects caused by minor schema drift, improve downstream analytics usability, and provide tenant-aware transformations and routing for Dedicated/Private customers. This service will live in the console ingestion path before enrichment and will emit validation metrics and drift signals to the analytics pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: New marshaller receives raw event payloads and emits a canonical envelope with type hints and a validation_status field (accepted | coerced | rejected).
Coercion rules are configurable per-tenant and per-event-type through existing schema-config store; default policy is soft-coerce for non-critical fields and reject on missing primary identifiers.
Metrics: per-event-type acceptance rate, coercion rate, and reject rate available in Console dashboard; perf target: <2ms median per-event marshalling at 10k eps per node.
Backfill plan documented and tested: when a new coercion rule is enabled, a dry-run is performed and warnings surfaced before wide rollout.
Canary rollout with 1% of traffic for one week and automatic rollback on >5% increase in downstream errors or >3x increase in latency.
End-to-end integration tests and a GitHub PR that passes CI and load checks are merged and reviewed by Platform and Analytics owners.
implementation_steps: Design API contract and canonical envelope (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Usage+Marshaller+Design).
Prototype coercion engine (Go) with pluggable rules and tenant overrides; implement unit tests for core transforms.
Integrate type-checker and fast-path for already-canonical payloads to avoid extra allocations.
Add metrics (prometheus) for acceptance/coercion/reject and histograms for processing latency.
Create migration/backfill job to reprocess 7 days of events in dry-run mode and produce a drift report.
Run performance benchmark at 50k eps simulated traffic and tune GC/serialization path.
Prepare canary run in us-west-2 for Console beta customers and monitor SLO dashboards.
comments: 2025-02-10 Asha Menon: Initial ticket created after weekly analytics sync. Priority set to P1 due to upcoming Dedicated customer onboarding that surfaced brittle event shapes.

2025-02-12 Diego Alvarez: Spike completed — proof-of-concept marshaller reduces hard rejects by ~68% in synthetic drift scenarios. Link to spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/eng/marshaller-spike.

2025-02-18 Platform review: Decided to adopt 'soft-typing' strategy — coerce when safe, reject when critical identity fields missing. Trade-off: slightly more downstream cleaning but fewer lost events. Documented reasoning in Confluence.
2025-02-22 UX/Analytics feedback (R. Chen): Add validation_status to envelope so dashboards can filter coerced vs native events. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-26 Diego Alvarez: Implemented initial coercion rule DSL, open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ingest/pull/482. Needs design review for rule semantics.
2025-03-01 Perf note: Microbenchmarks show median marshalling latency 1.8ms with object pooling; GC spikes at sustained 80k eps — next step tune allocator and consider JNI fast-path for hot fields.
2025-03-03 Security review request submitted for tenant override plumbing (PR comment). Waiting on infra confirmation for config encryption and RBAC for schema-config store.
2025-03-05 Diego Alvarez: Canaries scheduled for 2025-03-10 for 1% traffic. Dashboard link for canary monitoring: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console-marshaller/canary-overview.
notes: Fallback policy: when coercion fails and event is rejected, send to quarantine topic with sampling for manual inspection.
We will keep a short-lived audit trail for coerced fields marking original_value and final_value for debugging but redact PII in-flight.
Consider future extension: optional JSON Schema-based rule imports for third-party event shapes (post-RT).
